scenes.title: Wake Forest epilepsy suite: patient taps the remembered shape on a touchscreen as MIMO CA3-to-CA1 stimulation boosts recall 37%
scenes.era: 2018, Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center epilepsy monitoring unit, Winston-Salem

layout.description: Bright clinical hospital monitoring suite where a surgical epilepsy patient sits propped upright in an adjustable hospital bed with a clean white cranial wrap and fine ribbon leads connected to a bedside neural prosthetic computer; the patient reaches forward to tap the matching geometric photograph on a touchscreen tablet while the engineer's monitor displays synchronized CA3 input and MIMO-predicted CA1 output spike rasters.

positions.who: Surgical patient (mannequin in light blue hospital gown and clean white head bandage)
positions.where: seated upright in the hospital bed reaching a finger to tap the correct target image on an angled touchscreen

positions.who: Neuroscientist Robert Hampson (mannequin in white lab coat)
positions.where: standing beside the bedside MIMO computer cart
positions.facing: watching the CA3-to-CA1 spike translation display

props.name: over-bed touchscreen memory tablet
props.period_detail: mounted clinical touchscreen displaying four complex photographic shapes in the delayed match-to-sample test
props.physical_behavior: patient's index finger taps the exact remembered sample image and a green confirmation border lights up

props.name: bedside MIMO spike-translation workstation
props.period_detail: dual-trace display showing real-time CA3 input spikes on top and patterned CA1 stimulation pulses below
props.physical_behavior: CA1 pulse train fires in clean lockstep with the CA3 pattern

props.name: fine depth-electrode ribbon cable
props.period_detail: medical-grade multi-channel connector running from the clean head wrap to the amplifier

actions.verb_sequence: studies the sample image before it disappears -> waits through the delay screen -> reaches out and taps the exact matching image among distractors
points to the aligned CA3-to-CA1 spike raster as the patient's score rises 37 percent

reactions.reaction: nods with quiet satisfaction as delayed recognition stays sharp
exchange an amazed look beside the cart

scenes.wardrobe: Patient in clean light-blue hospital gown and neat white cranial wrap; researchers in white lab coat and Oxford shirt.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key clinical daylight streaming into the hospital monitoring room.
scenes.recognition_hook: A hospital patient playing a touchscreen memory game scores 37 percent higher when a computer plays his own hippocampal spike code back into layer CA1.

key_visual.description: the hospital patient taps the remembered image on a bedside touchscreen while the workstation translates CA3 spikes into CA1 pulses

scenes.title: Flat constant current vs patterned MIMO melody
scenes.era: 2018 USC / Wake Forest neural engineering comparison

layout.description: Clean neuroengineering lab bench comparing a flat metronome-pulse stimulator trace (zero gain) against the sparse spatiotemporal MIMO raster (+37% gain).

positions.where: standing at the wide waveform display
positions.facing: comparing scrambled pulses vs MIMO code

positions.where: standing beside a physical CA3-CA1 circuit board

props.name: comparison raster screen
props.period_detail: two side-by-side panels: flat/scrambled pulse train at 0% change vs MIMO spatiotemporal code at +37%
props.physical_behavior: MIMO trace aligns precisely with biological CA1 spikes

actions.verb_sequence: switches the display from scrambled control pulses to the personalized MIMO Volterra pattern

reactions.reaction: nods as only the timed biological pattern unlocks recall

scenes.wardrobe: Dark blazer and white lab coat.
